images.prompt:
Create one original photorealistic field-guide portrait of an anonymous mature Chilean Terrier, current national KCC2020 scope. Textual factual research only, no photograph input or named animal.

An anonymous mature male Chilean Terrier, national KCC2020 scope, about35cm at shoulder, balanced elegant firm near-square frame without heavy mass. White short smooth harsh close lustrous coat covers entire body, neck and full tail; symmetrical black-and-tan head/ears, tan brows/cheeks/inside ears and narrow white forehead blaze, no large trunk patches. Triangular head broad at base narrowing to strong clean muzzle slightly shorter than skull, flat moderately wide skull, subtle stop, tight lips/no heavy cheeks, dark small almond eyes and fully black nose. Natural small high-set thin V ears folded halfway with pointed ends toward outer eye corners, not erect or cropped. Moderately long muscular lightly arched neck without dewlap, high defined withers, short firm nearly straight back with very slight rearward slope, short strong slightly arched loin, moderately sloping muscular croup. Moderate chest almost to elbows, moderately sprung ribs and moderate abdominal tuck; chest depth45percent and leg length55percent of height. Four coherent straight foreleg courses with close elbows and short compact arched toes, muscular parallel hind legs/high hocks/catlike rear feet. Full natural moderately broad-rooted tail inserted LOW at croup but carried HIGH with a modest slight sickle curve, no longer than hock when lowered, smoothly tapering free endpoint clearly detached from body/backdrop. Tail never coils, forms ring, curls over back, lies flat over back, is bobbed/docked or cropped out.

New composition: right-facing three-quarter dog standing naturally on a broad dry rural gravel track. Modest low ochre hills, sparse olive-green distant shrubs and clear late-summer morning daylight; no copied show pose, handler, backdrop or source animal. Mouth closed, head gently toward viewer, balanced four grounded paws with clearly separate complete believable limb courses and anatomical joints. Full natural tail slightly to camera-facing side for entire attached root-to-free-tip course readable against uncluttered sky/hill, raised modest sickle without curling over back.

Sharp dog and contact shadows, softly blurred modest landscape. No vegetation/rocks covering paw contacts. No people, collar, leash, tags, gear, other dogs, props, fences, text, logos or watermark. No puppy proportions, erect ears, large body patches, bobtail, docked tail, ring tail, over-back curl or merged limbs.

profileEvidence.summary: The Chilean Terrier is described by its national standard as lively, alert and responsive, with reserve toward strangers. Its small-game and farm work included catching rodents. When rural families moved into towns in the late nineteenth century, they brought these dogs along to hunt rats around factories and shared housing.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A lively, alert Chilean farm terrier with a rat-catching tradition and a reserved response to strangers.
